overall_summary: Performance heavily clusters around space-based 'What If' scenarios and extreme planetary conditions published within the last 7 days. Videos featuring hypothetical space travel or bizarre planetary environments (e.g., liquid diamond, burning ice, darkest planet) achieve the highest views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes-per-view up to ~3.7%). Traditional flat facts underperform relative to immersive, experiential second-person thought experiments ('What If You Fell Into...').

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) achieved over 1,000 and 972 views rapidly with strong like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical planetary immersion hooks starting with 'What If You Fell Into...' or 'What If You Visited...' using extreme cosmic anomalies.

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre planetary extremes with visual hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing dark/unusual planets (e.g., 'The Planet Darker Than Coal', 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') maintain high sustained views and robust engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight extreme, counter-intuitive physical properties of newly discovered or lesser-known celestial bodies.

weak_patterns.pattern: Standard psychological and brain trivia without strong narrative stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' received low views (<60) and zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standalone psychological facts unless framed as a high-stakes neurological mystery or interactive test.

weak_patterns.pattern: Static historical or static biological trivia
weak_patterns.evidence: Older or static animal/history facts (e.g., 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever', 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery') show stagnant daily view velocity.
weak_patterns.action: Shift biological content toward cinematic survival dynamics or extreme physical adaptations rather than simple listicle facts.

next_video.concept: Journey into the center of a rogue planet with no star, where temperatures drop near absolute zero and sound travels through solid metallic hydrogen.
next_video.opening_direction: Start directly with the terrifying sensory experience of stepping onto a wandering planet lost in interstellar space with no sun in sight.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the crushing atmospheric pressure is actually turning your spacesuit into pure diamond while you fall toward a core made of super-dense fluid.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high-performing 'What If / Extreme Planet' cluster while introducing a completely fresh celestial phenomenon (rogue planets and metallic hydrogen).
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature diamond planets, burning ice, TrES-2b, or standard black holes.
Must use a newly introduced celestial body type (rogue planet / metallic hydrogen core).

experiment: Test a 21-second space 'What If' scenario focusing on an extreme interstellar rogue planet versus a standard planetary fact to confirm if second-person immersion consistently drives higher 7-day velocity.
